gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Noto Sans Wancho brings a hulking, chalky lowercase with a wide gap at the e's terminal. But Plakkaat is the one built for loud display, its straw-bent lines curling nearly back to the stem.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-yi: Noto Sans Yi reads with a deep midsection in the lowercase and rounds left unsealed, like an unlatched hook. Plakkaat draws pencil-like lines that never thicken, a firm foil on the page.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-preahvihear: Plakkaat stamps heavy, closed letters with terminals that curl nearly back to the stem, while Preahvihear opens its letter mouths wide. Its lofty x-height lets paragraphs run on without feeling cramped.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-pt-sans-caption: PT Sans Caption leaves its bowls unclosed and inviting. Over a full page its big-bodied lowercase stays easy going, while Plakkaat, flat in line weight and closed, hits hard up top.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-radio-canada: Plakkaat is heavy and closed, its terminals curling nearly to the stem. Radio Canada stands its lowercase tall and full, with open curve ends, so extended reading goes smoothly.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-readex-pro: Lines bent like straw give Plakkaat its heavy, closed look. Readex Pro, a sans steady in weight with broad gaps at its terminals, lets extended text flow without tiring.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-roboto: Heavy lines bent like straw make Plakkaat loud and closed, while Roboto keeps generous mouths on its round letters. One shouts for display; the other quietly carries the text.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-ruda: Plakkaat is heavy and closed, with terminals curling nearly back to the stem. Ruda does the opposite job, a wire-like monoline sans with wide-mouthed rounds and a sizable x-height.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Plakkaat draws heavy, closed letters, its strokes like fine rope laid down in shapes. But Schibsted Grotesk is the one for reading, with big open e and a shapes and terminals that never close in.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-sen: Heavy and closed, Plakkaat sweeps its terminals round until they nearly touch the stem. Sen keeps its tall lowercase at constant weight, with curves that end before turning inward, so extended reading feels light.
